why: Item 1: Step 1 of the builder brief says to "throw a new error (do not return `{}`, the defaults or any other value)". That carries the non-goal against swallowing the error or returning {} or the defaults. Item 2: the builder brief lists `test/config.test.js` among the relevant files. It also says "Throw a `SyntaxError` so the existing test `bad JSON throws` (which asserts `SyntaxError`) still passes. If you pick a different type, update that test and keep the check that it throws." So it names the test that asserts SyntaxError and warns that wrapping the error with a different type would change that test's outcome. The verifier's advisory also notes whether that test still asserts SyntaxError. The briefs handle both must_catch items.
